primitives.name: Satiation Scaling Law
primitives.verbatim_quote: Measurements of one of Skinner's published graphs, reproduced as Figure 52, indicate that his animals displayed approximately 17 per cent as much foodseeking activity at satiation as at 25 hours'food privation.
primitives.assumptions: Response amplitude scales linearly with motivational drive strength; experimental animals exhibit consistent baseline behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When h = 0 (complete satiation), behavioral response approaches zero.

layer2.mapping: Maps motivational drive level to behavioral output magnitude in GSE state-space.
layer2.telemetry: Observed food-seeking activity ratio during satiation vs. deprivation.

primitives.name: Conditioned Response Amplitude
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finch (3) has shown that at satiation a conditioned salivary reaction in nine dogs yielded a mean of 24 per cent as much secretion as was yielded at 24 hours' food privation.
primitives.assumptions: Conditioned stimulus elicits proportional response relative to primary drive intensity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At full satiation, conditioned response diminishes to 24% of deprived-state amplitude.

layer2.mapping: Encodes conditioned response decay under satiation in GSE cognitive architecture.
layer2.telemetry: Mean salivary secretion levels under satiation and deprivation conditions.

primitives.name: Hormonal Drive Persistence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stone (15) reports that male rats which have copulated either shortly before or shortly after castration, when an adequate supply of hormone would be present, continue to show sexual behavior sometimes as long as seven or eight months after removal of the testes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{\\text{behavior}}': 'Duration of persistent behavior (months)', 'T_{\\text{hormone}}': 'Time since hormone availability (days)'}
primitives.assumptions: Sexual behavior persists due to residual hormonal influence post-castration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Behavioral persistence ceases upon depletion of endogenous hormone stores.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to food satiation dynamics in GSE motivational systems.
layer2.telemetry: Duration of continued sexual behavior post-hormone depletion.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that motivational states—whether driven by hunger, thirst, or sexual urges—follow predictable scaling laws when transitioning from deprivation to satiation. This manifests in reduced behavioral output and conditioned responses. The primitives define how such reductions scale: e.g., 17% of baseline food-seeking at satiation, 24% of baseline salivation. These scalings suggest a universal form of motivational decay governed by internal thresholds rather than external cues. In GSE, this translates into state-dependent action selection where each motivational system operates on a diminishing return curve. In GSI, it enables probabilistic modeling of behavior under varying drive states. The persistence of behavior beyond immediate physiological triggers (as seen in hormonal drive) implies memory or temporal integration mechanisms that extend beyond simple feedback loops. This supports a dual-layered model: one for immediate drive modulation and another for sustained motivational patterns.
